tools.install: winget install Git.Git   (Git for Windows; the probe is tested against it)
winget install Rustlang.Rustup   (then: rustup default stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)
winget install astral-sh.uv   (runs make_large_tree.py and extract_failures.py)
winget install NASM.NASM   (the aws-lc-sys crates in quarto-hub need it)
winget install Kitware.CMake   (the aws-lc-sys crates in quarto-hub need it)
Visual Studio Build Tools, "Desktop development with C++" (cargo finds link.exe itself, so absent from PATH is normal; install only if the build says "linker not found")
fnm/nvm; Node major per .nvmrc (items b1 to b7)
optional: winget install jj-vcs.jj (the jj scenarios of b1 skip without it)

items.title: scripted end-to-end scenario against q2.exe and git.exe
items.reason: exit code 1; 0 passed, 1 failed; the transcript names the failing step
items.proves: The whole feature works end to end on Windows through the real q2.exe and git.exe on a generated repo in %TEMP% (about 4,000 tracked files): the gate pauses during a real git switch, the classifier treats a commit as a move-forward and a switch as a flip, a changed file flips, a removed file is unlisted, an added file is listed, a binary changes, arrival re-attaches the earlier docs without a fork, reset --hard keeps the dirty text in the retired doc, and a hub stopped during a switch skips the flush and leaves no conflict markers.
items.does_not_prove: jj on Windows; other Git builds; a long soak; the browser (c2 covers the editor surfaces).
